name: secure-dotfile
description: Find API keys and tokens written into your shell startup files and move the ones you pick into the macOS Keychain or the Linux secret service, without the agent seeing any value

interface.longDescription: Scans your zsh, bash, and fish startup files, .envrc, direnv env.d files, and the files they source for API keys, tokens, and passwords written as literal values. It lists each one by name, location, kind, and length, and says whether the value is in the file's git history. It moves only the items you pick into the macOS Keychain, or on Linux into the secret service through secret-tool, and changes each line to read the value from there when the shell starts, so programs keep the same environment variable. Scripts read and store the values, so the agent never sees any part of one. It re-checks each line before moving it, never overwrites a different value in the store, and runs the shell's syntax check on every edited file. Moving needs macOS, or Linux with secret-tool; scanning works anywhere.
defaultPrompt: Find API keys written into my shell config and move them to the Keychain
